as you wish.title: As you wish
as you wish.author: Cary Elwes
as you wish.why: Behind-the-scenes stories of making The Princess Bride, told warmly by one of its stars; a light, fun read for fans.

silence of the lambs.title: The Silence of the Lambs
silence of the lambs.author: Thomas Harris
silence of the lambs.why: An FBI trainee consults jailed Hannibal Lecter to catch a serial killer; a gripping, chilling thriller.

fates and furies.title: Fates and Furies
fates and furies.author: Lauren Groff
fates and furies.why: A marriage told from the husband's side and then the wife's; readers praise its compelling prose and twists.

nine billion names of god.title: The Nine Billion Names of God
nine billion names of god.author: Arthur C. Clarke
nine billion names of god.why: A short story about monks and a computer with a great final line; readers call it amazing.

dust.title: Dust
dust.author: Hugh Howey
dust.why: Final volume of the Silo trilogy, where the survivors face the truth about their world; a gripping dystopian read.

extremely loud and incredibly close.title: Extremely Loud and Incredibly Close
extremely loud and incredibly close.author: Jonathan Safran Foer
extremely loud and incredibly close.why: A nine-year-old wanders New York after losing his father on 9/11; inventive and moving, though some find it twee.

packing for mars.title: Packing for Mars
packing for mars.author: Mary Roach
packing for mars.why: A witty, informative look at the odd realities of human life in space; a Mary Roach favourite.

sure ill join your cult.title: Sure, I'll Join Your Cult
sure ill join your cult.author: Maria Bamford
sure ill join your cult.why: A comedian's honest, funny memoir about mental illness and recovery.

hotel new hampshire.title: The Hotel New Hampshire
hotel new hampshire.author: John Irving
hotel new hampshire.why: An eccentric family and its misfortunes across years and countries; a classic Irving mix of comedy and tragedy.

marriage portrait.title: The Marriage Portrait
marriage portrait.author: Maggie O'Farrell
marriage portrait.why: A young Renaissance duchess suspects her husband plans to kill her; vivid, though some like it less than Hamnet.

forsyte saga.title: The Forsyte Saga (The Man of Property / Indian Summer of a Forsyte / In Chancery / Awakening / To Let)
forsyte saga.author: John Galsworthy
forsyte saga.why: A long family saga of an English upper-class family; a Nobel-winning author's classic portrait of possession and society.

pull of the stars.title: The Pull of the Stars
pull of the stars.author: Emma Donoghue
pull of the stars.why: Three days in a Dublin maternity ward during the 1918 flu; moving, with a sharp sense of the era.

freshwater.title: Freshwater
freshwater.author: Akwaeke Emezi
freshwater.why: An autobiographical novel narrated by the multiple spirits within a young Nigerian woman; strange, intense and loved by readers.

city the city.title: The City & The City
city the city.author: China Miéville
city the city.why: A detective investigates a murder in two cities occupying the same space; a clever, weird mystery.

doctor zhivago.title: Doctor Zhivago
doctor zhivago.author: Boris Pasternak
doctor zhivago.why: A doctor-poet's life and love through the Russian Revolution; a banned Nobel-winning classic.

land remembered.title: A Land Remembered
land remembered.author: Patrick D. Smith
land remembered.why: Three generations of a Florida pioneer family; a beloved state classic for many readers.

dragon slippers.title: Dragon Slippers
dragon slippers.author: Jessica Day George
dragon slippers.why: A girl uses magical slippers and dragons to escape a bad fate; a charming childhood favourite.

spares.title: Spares
spares.author: Michael Marshall Smith
spares.why: A noir-tinged near-future about clones kept as spare body parts; recommended as a darker, strong read.

anna karenina by leo tolstoy.title: Anna Karenina
anna karenina by leo tolstoy.author: Leo Tolstoy
anna karenina by leo tolstoy.why: A married woman's affair and the lives around her in imperial Russia; a classic readers happily reread.

heartwood.title: Heartwood
heartwood.author: Amity Gaige
heartwood.why: A search for a missing hiker on the Appalachian Trail, told through several women's lives; readers find it absorbing.

play it as it lays.title: Play It as It Lays
play it as it lays.author: Joan Didion
play it as it lays.why: A numb Hollywood actress drifts through emptiness and despair; spare, haunting and highly praised.

bubblegum.title: Bubblegum
bubblegum.author: Adam Levin
bubblegum.why: Readers disagree, with one enjoying the self-indulgent style and another finding it mid, so no clear recommendation.

metamorphosis of prime intellect.title: The Metamorphosis of Prime Intellect
metamorphosis of prime intellect.author: Roger Williams
metamorphosis of prime intellect.why: An all-powerful AI grants immortality and reshapes human life; a disturbing online cult classic.

mill on the floss.title: The Mill on the Floss
mill on the floss.author: George Eliot
mill on the floss.why: A sister and brother grow up in a rural English community; readers are in awe of Eliot's depth.

another roadside attraction.title: Another roadside attraction
another roadside attraction.author: Tom Robbins
another roadside attraction.why: A quirky tale of hippies and a roadside zoo that find a stolen mummy; playful, witty and unconventional.

woom.title: Woom
woom.author: Duncan Ralston
woom.why: A very graphic horror novella that readers found queasy and disliked.

even cowgirls get the blues.title: Even Cowgirls Get the Blues
even cowgirls get the blues.author: Tom Robbins
even cowgirls get the blues.why: A hitchhiking woman with giant thumbs joins a ranch of cowgirls; a funny, wild counterculture novel.

this tender land.title: This Tender Land
this tender land.author: William Kent Krueger
this tender land.why: Orphans flee a boarding school and travel a river during the Depression; a warm, adventurous story.

time travellers wife.title: The Time Traveler's Wife
time travellers wife.author: Audrey Niffenegger
time travellers wife.why: A man involuntarily travels in time and loves the woman he keeps meeting; it makes readers cry.

this perfect day.title: This Perfect Day
this perfect day.author: Ira Levin
this perfect day.why: In a perfectly controlled dystopia, one man starts to question everything; a clever thriller by the Rosemary's Baby author.

emily wildes encyclopaedia of faeries.title: Emily Wilde's Encyclopaedia of Faeries
emily wildes encyclopaedia of faeries.author: Heather Fawcett
emily wildes encyclopaedia of faeries.why: A grumpy scholar studies faeries in a remote village; a cozy, charming fantasy that readers say pulls them out of slumps.

fools errand.title: Fool's Errand
fools errand.author: Robin Hobb
fools errand.why: The retired royal assassin Fitz is pulled back into court intrigue; a favourite among Robin Hobb fans.

alone.title: Alone
alone.author: Edgar Allan Poe
alone.why: The comments recommend different books with this name; it does not match the listed author or any clear recommendation.

sing unburied sing.title: Sing, Unburied, Sing
sing unburied sing.author: Jesmyn Ward
sing unburied sing.why: A family road trip in Mississippi haunted by ghosts and racism; painful but powerful.

middlemarch by george eliot.title: Middlemarch
middlemarch by george eliot.author: George Eliot
middlemarch by george eliot.why: A sweeping portrait of a provincial English town and the lives in it; a famous classic of the Victorian novel.

murder on the orient express.title: Murder on the Orient Express
murder on the orient express.author: Agatha Christie
murder on the orient express.why: Poirot investigates a murder on a snowbound train; a classic puzzle mystery with a famous twist.

random family.title: Random Family
random family.author: Adrian Nicole LeBlanc
random family.why: A reporter follows a Bronx family over a decade with intimate detail; readers say it is so good they wish to read it again.

shirley.title: Shirley
shirley.author: Charlotte Brontë
shirley.why: Charlotte Brontë's novel of industrial unrest and women's roles in Yorkshire; slower and less popular than Jane Eyre but interesting.

raptor red.title: Raptor Red
raptor red.author: Robert T. Bakker
raptor red.why: A year in the life of a raptor dinosaur, told as a novel by a palaeontologist.

climb.title: The Climb
climb.author: Anatoli Boukreev
climb.why: A guide's account of the 1996 Everest disaster, offering a different view from Into Thin Air.

broken sword.title: The Broken Sword
broken sword.author: Poul Anderson
broken sword.why: A Norse-inflected fantasy of elves, trolls and a cursed changeling; influential and grim.

god emperor of dune.title: God Emperor of Dune
god emperor of dune.author: Frank Herbert
god emperor of dune.why: Thousands of years later, Leto rules Dune as a tyrant; philosophical and divisive, fans find it fascinating.

market forces.title: Market Forces
market forces.author: Richard K. Morgan
market forces.why: Corporate executives settle deals with road-duels in a brutal near future; a savage satire from Richard Morgan.

strange case of dr jekyll and mr hyde.title: Strange Case of Dr Jekyll and Mr Hyde
strange case of dr jekyll and mr hyde.author: Robert Louis Stevenson
strange case of dr jekyll and mr hyde.why: A respectable doctor's experiment unleashes his violent double; a short classic of Victorian horror.

maia.title: Maia
maia.author: Richard Adams
maia.why: A long, lush tale set in the same world as Shardik, following a servant girl; loved by a small group of readers.

burning chrome.title: Burning Chrome
burning chrome.author: William Gibson
burning chrome.why: Gibson's cyberpunk short stories, including the origins of the Sprawl; stylish and influential.

book of lost things.title: The book of lost things
book of lost things.author: John Connolly
book of lost things.why: A grieving boy enters a dark fairy-tale world; known for a deeply moving ending.

changeling.title: The Changeling
changeling.author: Victor D. LaValle
changeling.why: A new father is pulled into a fairy-tale nightmare after a terrible event; readers couldn't put it down.

wishful drinking.title: Wishful Drinking
wishful drinking.author: Carrie Fisher
wishful drinking.why: Carrie Fisher's witty, candid account of fame, addiction and bipolar disorder; readers find it hilarious.

slade house.title: Slade House
slade house.author: David Mitchell
slade house.why: Every nine years, a visitor to a strange house in a small alley disappears; a creepy, quick haunted-house read.

journey to the center of the earth.title: Journey to the Center of the Earth
journey to the center of the earth.author: Jules Verne
journey to the center of the earth.why: A professor and his nephew climb down a volcano to the Earth's core; a classic adventure.

last picture show.title: The Last Picture Show
last picture show.author: Larry McMurtry
last picture show.why: Teenagers grow up in a dying Texas town in the 1950s; spare, bittersweet and sometimes uncomfortable.

maniac.title: The MANIAC
maniac.author: Benjamín Labatut
maniac.why: A fictionalised life of John von Neumann and the origins of modern computing and AI; fascinating and unsettling.

underland.title: Underland
underland.author: Robert Macfarlane
underland.why: A writer explores the worlds beneath the earth, from caves to nuclear tombs, blending science and myth.

molloy.title: Molloy
molloy.author: Samuel Beckett
molloy.why: Two broken narrators go in search of each other and their mother; experimental, with long unbroken paragraphs.

birds.title: The Birds
birds.author: Daphne du Maurier
birds.why: A short, eerie story of birds attacking a Cornish farming family; the basis for the Hitchcock film.

witches abroad.title: Witches Abroad
witches abroad.author: Terry Pratchett
witches abroad.why: Discworld witches travel to stop a fairy godmother's story; a funny parody of fairy tales.

book of three.title: The Book of Three
book of three.author: Lloyd Alexander
book of three.why: An assistant pig-keeper joins a quest against evil in a Welsh-inspired world; a children's fantasy classic.

american kingpin.title: American Kingpin
american kingpin.author: Nick Bilton
american kingpin.why: The story of the Silk Road dark-net market and its creator, told like a thriller; praised as top non-fiction storytelling.

tell me everything.title: Tell Me Everything
tell me everything.author: Elizabeth Strout
tell me everything.why: The comments mention it for other authors and books, so the match with Elizabeth Strout is unclear.

land of stories.title: The Land of Stories: The Wishing Spell
land of stories.author: Chris Colfer
land of stories.why: Twins fall into a fairy-tale world in this children's series; easy and enjoyable.

birdsong.title: Birdsong
birdsong.author: Sebastian Faulks
birdsong.why: A love story in pre-war France that turns into the horror of the trenches; devastating and unforgettable.

marrow.title: Marrow
marrow.author: Robert Reed
marrow.why: Explorers aboard a vast alien starship are trapped in a mystery with immortal crew; fans love its big ideas.

equal rites.title: Equal Rites
equal rites.author: Terry Pratchett
equal rites.why: A girl born a wizard in a world where only men can be; a funny early Discworld story.

go between.title: The Go-Between
go between.author: L. P. Hartley
go between.why: A boy delivers secret letters between lovers one hot summer; an elegant story of lost innocence.

small mercies.title: Small Mercies
small mercies.author: Dennis Lehane
small mercies.why: A Boston mother searches for her daughter during the 1974 busing crisis; a gripping crime novel.

desperation.title: Desperation
desperation.author: Stephen King
desperation.why: Travelers are trapped in a Nevada mining town ruled by an evil cop; readers say it pulled them in for days.

pawn of prophecy.title: Pawn of Prophecy
pawn of prophecy.author: David Eddings
pawn of prophecy.why: A farm boy sets out on a classic quest; simple, predictable, comforting fun.

into the drowning deep.title: Into the Drowning Deep
into the drowning deep.author: Mira Grant
into the drowning deep.why: A scientific expedition finds deadly mermaids; a quick and gory sea-monster thriller.

help.title: The Help
help.author: Kathryn Stockett
help.why: A popular book, but the comments mostly note it is disliked or controversial, so it is no clear recommendation.
